issues.legal_issue: The scope of the authority to prohibit contract labour at locations outside the site of industrial operations required determination by a Constitution Bench.
material_facts: A contractor employed workers to clean and sweep the Corporation’s staff housing colony and sports complex.
The High Court held that the workers were covered by a government notification abolishing contract labour and were entitled to absorption and employment benefits.
The Corporation challenged whether the prohibition could extend to work at those locations, which were not where its industrial operations were carried on.

An earlier Constitution Bench had discussed the scope of the prohibition, but the Court considered those observations not strictly necessary because that earlier case did not concern prohibition of contract labour.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not decide the scope of the prohibition. It referred for determination by a Constitution Bench whether the earlier observations were correct and whether the prohibition could extend to contract labour working at the staff housing colony and sports complex.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered that the earlier Constitution Bench’s observations about the scope of Section 10(1) and (2) of the Contract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) Act, 1970, in Gammon (India) Ltd. v. Union of India, were not strictly necessary to that decision, which did not concern prohibition of contract labour. The scope therefore required independent determination by a Constitution Bench.

predicates.appeal_from_high_court_order: A party appealed a High Court order concerning the treatment of contract workers.
predicates.dispute_concerns_scope_of_contract_labou: The parties disputed whether a prohibition on contract labour could cover workers at a location outside the site of industrial operations.
predicates.earlier_bench_observation_was_not_necess: An earlier larger bench discussed the disputed legal scope in a case that did not concern prohibition of contract labour.
predicates.scope_question_referred_to_constitution_: The court sends the disputed question of legal scope to a Constitution Bench for determination.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns the scope of a contract-labour prohibition and an earlier bench’s relevant observation was unnecessary to its decision, the scope question is referred to a Constitution Bench.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a notification abolishing contract labour covered cleaning and sweeping work at staff housing and a sports facility required determination by a Constitution Bench.
material_facts: A contractor employed workers to clean and sweep a staff housing colony and sports complex owned by the Corporation.
The High Court held that the workers were covered by the notification and were entitled to absorption and employment benefits.
The Corporation disputed whether the notification extended to work at those locations.
The Court considered the question important and concluded that the disputed coverage question should be determined by a Constitution Bench.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not decide whether the notification covered the workers. It referred that question to a Constitution Bench.
issues.legal_principle: The Court referred the question whether the notification dated 9 December 1976, issued under Section 10(1) of the Contract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) Act, 1970, validly abolished the contract labour in question. It did not determine the notification’s application on the merits.

predicates.appeal_from_high_court_order: A party appealed a High Court order concerning the treatment of contract workers.
predicates.notification_coverage_is_disputed: The parties disputed whether a notification abolishing contract labour covered workers performing services at staff housing and a sports facility.
predicates.coverage_question_requires_authoritative: The court considered the disputed coverage question important enough to require determination by a larger bench.
predicates.notification_coverage_question_referred_: The court sends the disputed question of notification coverage to a Constitution Bench for determination.

issues.definition: When an appeal involves disputed notification coverage and the question requires authoritative determination, the coverage question is referred to a Constitution Bench.
